question: outcome_summary
answer: The RFPP-S intervention showed significant effectiveness in improving mental health among youths with comorbid PTSD and suicidality. Participants experienced a 55% decrease in core PTSD symptoms and an 80% reduction in reactivity to trauma reminders. The RFPP-S group also had an 80% reduction in suicidal ideation, with a 100% adherence rate to follow-up visits. Additionally, there were no psychiatric readmissions due to suicidality in the RFPP-S group at one month, highlighting its effectiveness in treatment engagement and suicide prevention.

question: demographics_summary
answer: The study involved a total of 200 youths, with an average age of 13 years and a standard deviation of 2 years, indicating a focus on early adolescence. Gender distribution was similar across both groups, with 56% of the RFPP-S group being female and 58% of the control group being female. A significant aspect of the demographics is the prior treatment history, as 92% of participants had previous visits to psychiatric emergency rooms, and 72% had a history of psychiatric hospitalization. The majority of participants were on selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, with 88% in both groups receiving this medication.
